stem: The points $A$, $B$ and $C$ have coordinates $(-4,\,-1)$, $(2,\,7)$ and $(10,\,-1)$ respectively.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the equation of the line which passes through $C$ and is parallel to $AB$.
Give your answer in the form $ax + by = c$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
$OPQ$ is a triangle.
$\overrightarrow{OP} = \mathbf{p}$ and $\overrightarrow{OQ} = \mathbf{q}$.
$R$ is the point on $PQ$ such that $PR : RQ = 1 : 2$.
$S$ is the point on $OQ$ such that $OS : SQ = 1 : 2$.

subparts.label: (i)
subparts.text: Express $\overrightarrow{OR}$ in terms of $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$, as simply as possible.

subparts.label: (ii)
subparts.text: Express $\overrightarrow{SR}$ in terms of $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$, as simply as possible.

subparts.label: (iii)
subparts.text: Hence find $\dfrac{\text{area of triangle } QSR}{\text{area of triangle } QOP}$.

figure_description: A small sketch for part (d) only, labelled 'NOT TO SCALE'. Triangle OPQ with O at the bottom left, P at the bottom right (so OP is horizontal along the bottom) and Q above and slightly to the right of O, so that PQ slopes up to the left. R is marked on side PQ one third of the way from P to Q. S is marked on side OQ one third of the way from O to Q. The line segment SR is drawn (it will look parallel to OP; that is inherent in the configuration and nothing is written about it). Side OP carries a single arrowhead from O to P labelled p in bold; side OQ carries a single arrowhead from O to Q labelled q in bold. The vertices are labelled O, P, Q, R, S in upright capitals. No ratios, no lengths, no fractions, no other arrows and no vector expressions are printed on the figure. Parts (a), (b) and (c) have no figure.
solution:
(a) Gradient of $AB = \frac{7 - (-1)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}$
The required line is parallel to $AB$, so its gradient is also $\frac{4}{3}$, and it passes through $C(10,\,-1)$:
$y - (-1) = \frac{4}{3}(x - 10)$
$3(y + 1) = 4(x - 10)$
$3y + 3 = 4x - 40$
$4x - 3y = 43$
Check with $C$: $4(10) - 3(-1) = 40 + 3 = 43$.

(b) $AB = \sqrt{(2 - (-4))^{2} + (7 - (-1))^{2}} = \sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ units

(c) $A(-4,\,-1)$ and $C(10,\,-1)$ have the same $y$-coordinate, so $AC$ is horizontal.
Base $AC = 10 - (-4) = 14$ units.
The perpendicular height from $B$ to $AC$ is $7 - (-1) = 8$ units.
Area of triangle $ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 8 = 56$ units$^2$

(d)(i) $\overrightarrow{PQ} = \overrightarrow{OQ} - \overrightarrow{OP} = \mathbf{q} - \mathbf{p}$
Since $PR : RQ = 1 : 2$, $\overrightarrow{PR} = \frac{1}{3}\overrightarrow{PQ} = \frac{1}{3}(\mathbf{q} - \mathbf{p})$
$\overrightarrow{OR} = \overrightarrow{OP} + \overrightarrow{PR} = \mathbf{p} + \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{q} - \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{p} = \frac{2}{3}\mathbf{p} + \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{q}$

(d)(ii) Since $OS : SQ = 1 : 2$, $\overrightarrow{OS} = \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{q}$
$\overrightarrow{SR} = \overrightarrow{OR} - \overrightarrow{OS} = \frac{2}{3}\mathbf{p} + \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{q} - \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{q} = \frac{2}{3}\mathbf{p}$

(d)(iii) $\overrightarrow{SR} = \frac{2}{3}\overrightarrow{OP}$, so $SR$ is parallel to $OP$ and $SR = \frac{2}{3}OP$.
Triangles $QSR$ and $QOP$ share the angle at $Q$, and angle $QSR = $ angle $QOP$ (corresponding angles, $SR \parallel OP$), so the triangles are similar with $\frac{SR}{OP} = \frac{2}{3}$.
$\frac{\text{area of triangle } QSR}{\text{area of triangle } QOP} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{2} = \frac{4}{9}$
Check by common heights: triangles $QSR$ and $QOR$ have the common vertex $R$ with bases $QS$ and $QO$ on the same line, so $\frac{\text{area } QSR}{\text{area } QOR} = \frac{QS}{QO} = \frac{2}{3}$; triangles $QOR$ and $QOP$ have the common vertex $O$ with bases $QR$ and $QP$ on the same line, so $\frac{\text{area } QOR}{\text{area } QOP} = \frac{QR}{QP} = \frac{2}{3}$. Hence $\frac{\text{area } QSR}{\text{area } QOP} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{9}$, as before.
syllabus_check: Every part sits inside 4052. (a) gradient of the line joining two points and the equation of a straight line through a given point parallel to a given line (parallel lines have equal gradients), rearranged to ax + by = c with integer coefficients — one 3-mark part, no separate mark for the gradient. (b) length of a line segment by Pythagoras' theorem (the 6-8-10 triple keeps it exact). (c) area of a triangle by base x height using a horizontal side as the base — no shoelace formula and no midpoint formula. (d) vectors in two dimensions: a point dividing a side in a given ratio, expressing OR and SR in terms of p and q by vector addition and scalar multiples, then the deduction that SR is parallel to OP with SR = (2/3)OP; the area ratio follows either by similar triangles (area scale factor = square of the length scale factor, Congruency and Similarity) or purely by the vectors-section rule for triangles with a common vertex and bases on the same line, both within 4052. Calculator allowed as the rubric states; every answer is exact so no precision statement is needed. No 3-D vectors, no calculus, no surds.
originality_note: The exemplars build a trapezium OACB whose area gives a quadratic (2025 Q8), a k-and-p intersection plus a 25-unit length with a negative unknown (2024 Q3), a PQ-and-PR coordinate triangle followed by an OCD triangle with a point X fixed by a parallel condition and XD wanted (2022 Q8), or an OAB triangle with a 2:3 point and two midpoints leading to naming a quadrilateral (2023 specimen Q6). This question's coordinate half is a single triangle ABC with a parallel line through the third vertex, an exact length and an area by a horizontal base; its vector half is a fresh OPQ triangle with both dividing points given as 1:2 ratios (no midpoints, no parallel condition given — the parallel is what the candidate discovers) ending in a ratio of areas of two triangles, 4/9, a sequence none of the exemplars follows. The points (-4,-1), (2,7), (10,-1), the line 4x - 3y = 43, the area 56, the vectors (2/3)p + (1/3)q and (2/3)p and the ratio 4/9 were all chosen and derived from scratch and checked (the area ratio two ways), and no exemplar number, unknown or part order is reused.
